questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.**

The students are in ______ of their teachers.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **awe**.

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The correct word that fits the blank contextually is **Awe** which means feelings of respect and either fear or admiration (भय या प्रशंसा से प्रेरित आदर भाव__).

 __
 
• Example: *As a young boy he was very much in **awe **of__ his uncle.​*
 
 
 
• "be in awe of/stand in awe of" is a prepositional phrase.
 
• If you are in awe of someone or if you stand in awe of them, you have a lot of respect for them and are slightly afraid of them.
 
• Hence. we can say that the correct choice is** option 2**.

 

*The correct sentence would be: The students are in awe of their teachers.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• Praise: appreciation, cheer, commendation
 
• Respect: regard, consideration, thoughtfulness
 
• Gusto: enthusiasm

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No Improvement.**

The wound on her hand __is now heal__ completely.
questions.solution:
The underlined phrase must be replaced with **has now healed.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

We use the present perfect tense of a verb when we refer to an event that has occurred in the recent past. Thus, 'heal' is replaced with the past participle form 'healed'.

Options 1 & 4 are grammatically incorrect.

The correct usage will be: *The wound on her hand has now healed completely.*

questions.question:
**Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.**

The child always goes for sleep with his teddy bear.
questions.solution:
The erroneous part is** 'goes for sleep'**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **error** is in the **second part **of the sentence.

 
 
• Sleep is an intransitive verb and hence will be in the 1st person singular form 'sleeps'.
 
• We generally use the phrase 'go to sleep'. Hence, 'for' must be replaced with 'to'
 
• Also 'always' denotes a regular activity.
 
 

The correct sentence will be: *The child always goes **to sleep** with his teddy bear.*
